title: Optimize: wire recommendation ROI estimates to Standard Cost Model outputs
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Objective
Wire Optimize ROI calculations (batching/caching/quantization recommendations) to the Standard Cost Model v1 outputs so that Optimize, Console, and finance reporting share the same primitives.

Background / Why
Optimize currently computes ROI using a mix of telemetry-derived heuristics and prototype cost curves. This has caused:
- ROI numbers that do not match Console cost breakdowns.
- Support escalations where “what-if savings” look optimistic vs observed spend.
- Ongoing drift whenever runtime instrumentation or billing hooks change.

This ticket migrates Optimize to call Cost Model API what-if endpoints and consume the standardized breakdown taxonomy (prefill vs decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, overhead allocation, quantization deltas).

Scope (v1)
1) Replace Optimize’s internal cost estimator with Cost Model API v1 for ROI computations.
2) Implement a mapping layer: RecommendationConfig -> CostModelWhatIfRequest.
3) Update ROI outputs to include standardized breakdown fields and confidence/guardrail messaging.
4) Roll out behind a feature flag and validate against backtests.

Non-goals
- Changing pricing or invoicing logic.
- Building customer-facing calculators.
- Adding new what-if dimensions beyond those exposed by Cost Model API v1.

Implementation Plan
A) Integration surface
- Use cost-model client library (ENG-4830) with schema version negotiation.
- Call endpoint: POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if (exact route per design spec; keep implementation behind client abstraction).
- Provide 2 inputs per ROI calculation:
  1) Baseline workload summary (observed): request rate distribution, prompt/output token distributions, cache stats if known.
  2) Proposed configuration delta (recommendation): e.g., batching target, cache policy change, quantization profile ID.

B) Mapping: Optimize Recommendation -> What-if request
Create a single adapter module in Optimize backend:
- Map recommendation types:
  - Batching: target_batch_size or batching_policy_id -> what-if batching parameters
  - Caching: prefix cache enablement + expected hit rate bounds -> what-if caching parameters (bounded; no per-customer high-cardinality keys)
  - Quantization: map model + quant_profile_id from model catalog -> what-if quantization parameters
- Ensure we pass deployment context:
  - hosted/dedicated/private
  - region / hardware sku (if known)
  - runtime execution path id (if provided by telemetry)
- Handle missing/unknown fields:
  - If Optimize cannot provide cache hit rate, use “unknown” and rely on Cost Model default assumptions (must be surfaced in ROI explanation).
  - If quant profile ID is missing, do not attempt quant ROI; emit “not applicable” reason.

C) ROI calculation logic changes
Old (prototype): estimated $/1K tokens * delta_tokens * utilization fudge factors.
New (standard):
- Use Cost Model output fields:
  - baseline_total_cost
  - proposed_total_cost
  - breakdown_by_stage: prefill, decode
  - breakdown_by_attribution: request_attributable vs overhead_allocated
  - breakdown_by_effect: cache_savings, batch_efficiency_delta, quantization_delta
- Compute ROI:
  - savings_absolute = baseline_total_cost - proposed_total_cost
  - savings_percent = savings_absolute / baseline_total_cost
  - payback_period (if recommendation requires engineering work) uses configured effort multipliers (existing Optimize concept) but cost delta is authoritative.

D) Confidence / uncertainty handling
- Consume any confidence interval fields from Cost Model what-if response (if present in v1). If absent:
  - Use deterministic values but label ROI “Model estimate” and show sensitivity when assumptions are “unknown” (e.g., cache hit rate).
- Guardrails:
  - If Cost Model returns “bounded/invalid” due to policy guardrails, surface user-friendly reason and disable “Apply” CTA.

E) Performance and request bounding
- Batch ROI calls per page load (Optimize UI often displays a list of recommendations). Proposed approach:
  - Per workload_id, compute once and cache in Optimize for 10–30 minutes.
  - Use request bounding guidance from Cost Model API guidelines (no unbounded breakdown dimensions).
- Timeouts/retries:
  - Use client defaults; hard timeout 500ms (Optimize does not require per-request synchronous correctness at the expense of latency).
  - On failure: fallback to “ROI unavailable (degraded)” rather than old estimator (to avoid reintroducing inconsistency). PM decision needed on whether we prefer stale last-known-good.

Acceptance Criteria
- Optimize ROI numbers are derived exclusively from Cost Model API v1 under flag optimize.costModelRoi.enabled.
- Recommendation payloads include:
  - baseline_total_cost, proposed_total_cost, savings_absolute, savings_percent
  - top-level breakdown fields required for UI explanation (prefill/decode split at minimum)
  - explanation of missing assumptions (e.g., cache hit rate unknown)
- Backtest on 3 representative workloads shows delta within agreed thresholds vs observed spend attribution (using validation harness fixtures).
- Metrics:
  - % ROI calculations using cost-model by schema version
  - cost-model call p95 latency + error rate
  - % recommendations with “ROI unavailable”

Risks / Open Questions
- Cache warm-rate assumption: Cost Model v1 does not accept “warm rate” as a first-class parameter (per platform pushback). We should avoid inventing a local knob. For v1, treat warm/cold as bounded hit-rate ranges and document clearly.
- Overhead allocation: Finance wants overhead to be visible but not over-interpreted. Optimize should default ROI to include overhead_allocated for consistency with Console, but UI text must clarify.
- Drift: if telemetry lag impacts baseline workload summary, ROI may jump. Mitigate by using a stable lookback window and surfacing timestamp.

Links
- Confluence PRD: /product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd
- Design spec: /product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec
- ADR taxonomy: /architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy
- Integration references:
  - Console adoption ticket: ENG-4825
  - What-if endpoint ticket: ENG-4824
  - Client library ticket: ENG-4830

Rollout Plan
1) Implement adapter + ROI compute changes behind feature flag.
2) Run backtests in staging with golden fixtures; compare vs prior ROI + observed spend.
3) Enable for internal users only (Optimize team + CS) for 1 week.
4) Ramp to 5% of prod orgs; monitor “ROI unavailable”, latency, and drift dashboards.
5) Full rollout; remove legacy estimator codepath after 2 release cycles.
comments: 2026-01-17 (Aditya Rao): Optimize needs at minimum: prefill vs decode split, cache savings attribution, and quantization delta. If v1 can’t model cache warm-up directly, we can ship with a conservative assumption and message it clearly. Please do not block on new parameters; ship v1 and capture v2 asks separately.

2026-01-22 (Ethan Park): What-if endpoint will enforce strict bounds (no per-request token histograms beyond fixed buckets). Use workload_summary with capped bucket counts. Also, please use the client library for version negotiation; we expect schema tweaks during rollout.

2026-02-03 (Jonas Weber): For confidence, we can accept deterministic output in v1 but we should surface “sensitivity” when cache hit rate is unknown. Suggest: show a range using min/max hit-rate bounds if cost-model can accept bounds; otherwise label as 'assumes current hit rate'.

2026-02-08 (Hassan Mirza): Implemented adapter for batching + quantization. Caching mapping is blocked pending clarification on which cache metrics are stable from telemetry (KV vs prefix cache). For now using prefix_cache_hit_rate from workload summary when present; otherwise passing unknown.

2026-02-12 (Sofia Ivanova): Reminder: batch_efficiency from runtime differs from 'batch size'. Don’t pass target_batch_size as a proxy for efficiency; instead let cost-model compute efficiency delta based on scheduling model. If you pass a policy id, it’s better than a numeric batch size.

2026-02-18 (Marissa Cole): Console will show overhead_allocated explicitly. Optimize ROI should match that default to avoid another mismatch ticket; if you want request-only ROI, make it a secondary view (not default).

2026-02-20 (Hassan Mirza): PR up for review to switch ROI computation to cost-model what-if results and remove legacy estimator fallback. Added flag optimize.costModelRoi.enabled, metrics, and 'ROI unavailable' UI state. Requesting review from Platform + Applied ML.
activity: 2026-01-16: Ticket created by Talia Benson after v1 scope alignment; assigned to Hassan Mirza.
2026-01-23: Dependency added on ENG-4830 (client library) after API shape discussion in platform thread.
2026-02-05: Marked In Progress; adapter module scaffolded and unit tests added for mapping edge cases (unknown cache hit rate, missing quant profile id).
2026-02-14: Staging validation run completed on two workloads; one showed ~6% higher savings than expected due to overhead handling. Updated to include overhead_allocated by default.
2026-02-20: Marked In Review; awaiting approvals and final backtest run with latest cost-model service build.
